# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 18 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 10

**1** She showed me a great multitude of people approaching from afar, and in their midst a man of extraordinary height — taller than the tower itself — in appearance like the master of a great estate, with a magnificent crown on his head and clothed in gleaming white garments. **2** He wore white boots on his feet; in his right hand he held a sickle, in his left a shepherd's crook. He came and stationed himself before the tower. **3** He directed that the stones be brought and fitted into the building. Six young men who were building, along with four others on his right, received the stones and continued the work. **4** He then ordered the workers who had been hauling stones to reject them all and cast them far from the tower. Yet not a single stone lying near the tower was rejected — they were all placed in the building because they were smooth and shining. **5** However, many were rejected from the large numbers that lay far away. He directed these to be stacked in separate heaps — some in one pile, some in another, some in a third. But the twelve mountains were not piled up; they were arranged in order according to their individual appearance. **6** When the stones had been set in the building, the man called out to me: "Come here, Hermas." I approached and said, "My lord, do you call me?" He replied, "What would you like to know?" "Lord," I said, "I want to understand the whole vision from beginning to end — especially the stones placed in the building, the ones rejected, the ones thrown far away, and why the building has not yet been finished."

---

*LOGOS note: The great lord with sickle and crook combines harvest imagery (sickle = judgment/reaping) with pastoral imagery (crook = shepherd/care). Together they identify him as Christ — judge and shepherd.*
